title: Billing edge cases for interleaved prefetch and KV batching
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Concrete problem: we have observed inconsistent billing and quota accounting when requests that would hit the prefix/KV cache are interleaved with prefetch and coalesced batches. In particular: (1) token charges are sometimes duplicated across the originating request and a downstream cached-prefetch ticket when prefetch races with a serving batch; (2) rate limit counters are decremented by batched aggregator units that later get short-circuited by a KV cache hit, causing quotas to under-report consumption; (3) accounting for prefix matches across multi-tenant pools can attribute savings to the wrong customer when batches are aggregated across routing boundaries. This ticket defines the detection, deterministic attribution rules, and billing pipeline changes required to make metering and rate-limit accounting correct and auditable for these edge cases.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce explicit 'billing-intent' tags on request lifecycles: originator, prefetch, coalesced-aggregate. Billing will only attribute token charges to the originator tag unless a later request with a different originator consumes previously uncharged tokens. 2) Implement a small time-windowed aggregation key for batched groups (batch_group_id) that is persisted to the metering event at the time of batch execution; when a KV cache short-circuits after batch execution, emit a compensating billing event instead of retroactively deleting charges. 3) Decouple rate-limit counters from billing events: rate-limit tokens will continue to be consumed at request ingress using a conservative estimate, but the billing pipeline will reconcile consumption with final execution using deterministic compensation events. 4) Route-aware attribution: add tenant routing metadata to batch_group_id so that cross-tenant aggregation does not co-mingle billing attribution. 5) Add an idempotent event schema for billing records including fields: request_id, batch_group_id, billing_intent, billed_tokens, cache_result (HIT/MISS/PARTIAL), and reconciliation_flag. 6) Audit trail: store original and compensating events for 30 days with query helpers to reconstruct per-request billing. Implementation will be incremental behind a feature flag with a migration that replays 30 days of recent events to backfill batch_group_id for historical analysis.
tradeoffs: - Pros: deterministic accounting, easier audits, correct customer billing, reduced disputes. - Cons: additional storage for compensating events and batch metadata, slight increase in latency to attach batch_group_id at batch execution, complexity in reconciliation logic. Alternative: retroactively delete erroneous bill events but that risks holes in audit trails and is less robust for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: All unit and integration tests for billing reconciliation pass
End-to-end test where a prefetch races with a batch results in a single billed token for the originator in 1000 synthetic runs
Rate-limit counters remain monotonic and reconciliation events do not cause deficits (no negative usage) in staging
Queryable audit trail returns consistent request->billing mappings for 30-day window
Performance: average batch latency increase <= 1ms after adding batch_group_id assignment
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated implementation deployed to staging (billing-2025.03.feature-prefetch-accounting)
Smoke tests in staging with sampled traffic including multi-tenant batches
Gradual rollout to 5% of production traffic for 48 hours with realtime metrics (billing_discrepancies, reconciliations_emitted)
Expand to 25% then 100% contingent on no high-severity discrepancies
Backfill job run to compute batch_group_id for last 30 days for offline analytics (run in low-traffic window)
Post-rollout: 7-day observation window and postmortem if discrepancies > 0.01% of calls
testing_notes: Create synthetic workload that interleaves prefetch, originator request, and coalesced batches with random scheduling jitter
Inject KV cache hits at several offsets (immediate, 2ms, 10ms) to validate compensating-event emission
Fuzz tests for batch_group_id collisions and tenant routing mismatches
Add property-based tests that assert conserved token accounting (sum of billed_tokens == actual executed tokens +/- permitted delta)
implementation_tasks: Add batch_group_id field to runtime batch executor and persist to metering proto
Emit compensating billing events when cache short-circuits after batch execution
Update rate-limit service to write conservative ingress counters and expose reconciliation API
Add tenant metadata to batching router to prevent cross-tenant meter mixing
Update billing pipeline consumer to apply idempotent reconciliation logic and store audit trail
Create backfill job and dashboard for historical reconciliation metrics
notes: Observed discrepancies first reported by Solutions Eng on 2025-01-18 for a large customer running prefix-heavy prompts
Spike results: local shim reproduced duplicate-billing 7/100 runs when prefetch and batch race
Cost estimate for storage: ~200GB/month for compensating events at current volume
